reason: The text actually demonstrates the opposite of this statement. The narrative shows Egypt's elite institutions (Pharaoh's magicians and wise men) completely unable to interpret the dreams, while Joseph—a Hebrew slave imprisoned in Egypt—succeeds where all the elite have failed. Joseph's wisdom is explicitly attributed to God ('אלהים יענה' - 'God will answer'), not to inherent elite status. His elevation to power is presented as meritocratic, based on demonstrated divine wisdom and capability rather than birth or prior social standing. The passage undermines rather than supports the notion that the elite are inherently superior.
